thread:
maira: quick RFC follow-up — I'd like to propose a 'probabilistic holdback' layer in the proxy for A/B canaries. idea: majority of flips remain deterministic by policy, but we inject a small randomized holdback factor so that not all hosts flip at the same time under transients. less blast radius + smooth ramp. thoughts?

jon: sounds interesting. how deterministic do we need the audits to be? randomized flips sound scary for replay/debugging.

liz: two quick mitigations: 1) make the RNG seed derivable from decision_id + policy_version so replay is deterministic for a given event; 2) log the seed and the sampled decision in the compact decision event. that keeps reproducibility while still spreading flips in time.

sam: main ops concern: if holdback causes uneven latency for a tenant (some requests go to safe variant, others to new), that can confuse product metrics. need a way to correlate user requests to decision contexts in telemetry.

maira: agreed — we should attach a short decision_context token (opaque) to requests so downstream metrics can be correlated. that token is ephemeral and avoids leaking tenant info.

jon: implementation sketch: LocalDecider evaluates local score (p50 latency, error-rate, queue-depth) into a single composite metric, applies policy thresholds, then a damping function: final_decision = policy_decision unless rand(seed) < holdback_prob. We should gate holdback_prob by traffic_fraction threshold: only apply for small flips (<5% traffic) maybe.

liz: also propose a leaky-bucket flip_quota per-proxy to ensure a single host can't flip 100% of its traffic multiple times in a minute. keeps thrash low.

sam: about control plane: central still publishes authoritative policy versions, a safety_fence epoch, and a "drift advisory" signal (estimates of cluster-wide congestion). proxies must ignore stale safety_fence epochs. central can also set a global default holdback_profile but allow tenant overrides.

ops-bot: FYI: created alert template "holdback-imbalance" and added checklist entry "ensure decision_context token available in traces".

maira: config example (pseudo, for RFC):
```
policy_id: p-prob-holdback-v1
thresholds:
  latency_p50: 200ms
  error_rate: 0.02
holdback:
  enabled: true
  seed_salt: "policy-v1"
  base_prob: 0.15
  max_for_large_flip: 0.05
damping:
  flip_quota_per_min: 2
  recovery_window_s: 90
```

jon: lifecycle: policy rollouts must be versioned and support preview mode — central publishes new policy_version in preview state and we can sample a tiny % of proxies for evaluation. also require canary policy changes to be reversible by central override.

liz: audit trail: compact decision events (decision_id, policy_version, seed, inputs_hash, chosen_variant, rationale) should be produced to the eventbus. keep them compact and compressed. add quick replay tool that can reconstruct decisions deterministically.

sam: edge-case: partitioned guidance stream. proxies must fallback to default holdback_profile on-disk and operate autonomously. include a safe-mode that disables probabilistic holdback (switches to conservative deterministic policy) after N failed guidance heartbeats.

maira: one more thought: for large traffic flips (>T% of tenant traffic) require a lightweight quorum handshake: peers in same AZ respond with vote; if quorum says OK, permit flip. this prevents a single misbehaving host from flipping too much. keep quorum size small and timeout short.

jon: sounds good. who owns tuning? suggest runtime owns default profiles, SRE owns safety_fences and alerting, product defines acceptable UX tradeoffs.

liz: next steps: maira to put together RFC with state diagram for holdback + deterministic replay plan, message contracts for guidance/override, and a short operator runbook for chaos (partitioned control plane, clock skew, heavy load). tag runtime/sre/observability.

maira: will do — target RFC draft by Thurs. thanks all :thumbsup:
